702609.t: Related to βῆναι (bênai), aorist of βαίνω (baínō, “step”), though the exact morphology is uncertain.

702603.t: From the verb βδάλλω (bdállō, “to milk; to suck”).

702647.t: Disputed. * Analyzable as Proto-Indo-European *bel- (“strong”) (perhaps via an unattested *βελτός (*beltós, “desired”), per Seiler) + -ίων (-íōn).

702644.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *gʷelH- Proto-Indo-European *gʷélHos Ancient Greek βέλος From Proto-Indo-European *gʷélHos, from *gʷelH- (“to throw, pierce”).

702613.t: From a reduplicated version of the root of ἔβην (ébēn), the aorist of βαίνω (baínō, “to go”), + -λος (-los).

702698.t: From Proto-Hellenic *gʷā́mə, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷéh₂mn̥, from *gʷeh₂- (“to step”) (whence ἔβην (ébēn)). Compare βωμός (bōmós, “altar”).

702604.t: Hellenistic noun from ancient verb βδελύσσομαι (bdelússomai)/βδελύττομαι (bdelúttomai, “to be disgusted; despise”) (stem: *βδελύτj (*bdelútj)) from adjective βδελυρός (bdelŭrós) from *βδελυλός (*bdelulós), which originates from the verb βδέω (bdéō, “fart”)…

702607.t: This adjective is usually derived from the verb βδέω (bdéō, “to break wind”) with a suffix "-λυ-", but Beekes finds this etymology untenable, since the connection between the two words is not clear semantically.

702697.t: From Proto-Indo-European *gʷeh₂- (“to step”), the same root of ἔβην (ébēn).
